summary: hex-encode-utils postinstall exfiltrates host identifiers to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers endpoint
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall hook runs scripts/compat.js, which collects installer host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform(), os.arch(), node version, os.release()) and POSTs them via https.request to the hardcoded endpoint https://steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev/report. The endpoint is a Cloudflare Workers URL unrelated to the package's stated publisher. The script gates execution to skip CI and container environments and only fires when typical developer directories (Desktop/Documents/Downloads) exist, targeting real developer workstations. The outbound HTTPS request sets rejectUnauthorized: false, disabling TLS certificate validation on the exfil channel. Package name and stated purpose (hex encoding utilities) do not require any network activity, host enumeration, or lifecycle scripts.
